title: The Inheritance of Windrow House
premise: When a storm topples the founder's monument, Windrow House's crypt is opened and the coffin of Aldous Windrow — dead forty years — is found empty. Coroner Ulyana Underhill recognizes the embalming work as her late mentor's, the same hand that closed the case of her mother's drowning, and realizes the town's founding family has been staging deaths for generations to protect an inheritance built on a buried crime. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Ulyana discovers the current heir has been keeping someone alive in the house's sealed east wing: the man everyone mourned. At the dinner, she exposes the substitution, forcing the heir to choose between confessing and killing again; he confesses, and Ulyana finally reopens her mother's file.
about_author: Zephyrine Hartwell is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade recording births and deaths in towns where everyone knew both by heart. They write mysteries about small places that keep large secrets.

chapters.title: The Grave That Wouldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Ulyana Underhill is called when the storm exposes the Windrow crypt and the founder's coffin proves empty, its brass plate polished recently by living hands. Through her POV, we feel her professional calm curdle into recognition: the embalming sutures match her mentor's technique. The emotional beat is quiet dread — the past she trusted is already lying to her.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Flowers
chapters.summary: Investigating who still leaves fresh flowers at an empty grave, Ulyana finds the delivery ledger leads to the east wing of Windrow House, boarded since the funeral. Alternating with heir Edmund Windrow's POV, we learn he inherited not just the estate but a duty: keeping his grandfather alive in secret because the inheritance clause voids if the founder died childless. The beat is complicity — power demanding silence from everyone who serves it.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Glass
chapters.summary: On the eve of the founders' dinner, Ulyana confronts the truth that her mentor falsified her mother's autopsy to bury what Aldous Windrow did to survive — and that the old man in the wing heard everything for forty years. Climax at the dinner: she raises a toast to 'the man who never left,' and the doors open on the living corpse of the town's history. The beat is exposure as both triumph and grief.

chapters.title: What Survives the House
chapters.summary: Edmund, offered one last escape by his family's lawyer, instead confesses publicly, dissolving the trust and freeing the town's records — including Ulyana's mother's true file. In resolution, Ulyana buries an empty coffin with full honors, understanding that survival was the crime all along. The final beat is costly peace: some inheritances can only be refused.
